previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, multiple abdominal surgeries, and recurrent paralytic ileus was admitted for worsening abdominal pain and vomiting over one week. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and electrolyte replacement for hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. Imaging showed no bowel obstruction but supported a diagnosis of paralytic ileus, with evidence of slow contrast transit. A possible digestive-genital tract fistula was noted, along with mild metabolic acidosis and venous compression, both of which stabilized during the admission. Urine cultures showed no infection. The patient gradually improved, passing flatus and tolerating oral intake, allowing NG tube removal and discharge home. She was advised to continue supplements, avoid opioids, and follow up with gastroenterology and primary care for ongoing management of Crohn’s, fistula, and mental health concerns including depression and PTSD.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ with crohn's, multiple surgeries, s/p cholecystectomy,
allergy to IV contrast.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the lesser
trochanters after administration of oral contrast only. Coronal and sagittal
reformations were prepared.

DOSE:  DLP: 856 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

Lungs and Heart: There is very minimal atelectasis is of the right middle
lobe.  The heart and pericardium are normal appearing.

Liver, Gallbladder: The liver is normal in size and attenuation. There are no
focal hepatic mass is identified. The hepatic and portal veins are normal for
and appear patent.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.

Spleen: The spleen is normal in size and enhancement.

Pancreas: The pancreas shows normal enhancement. There is no pancreatic duct
dilatation or peripancreatic fat stranding.

Kidneys, Adrenals: The kidneys display symmetric nephrograms with no evidence
of hydronephrosis or mass lesion in either kidney.  The ureters are
symmetrical in their course to the bladder.
 The adrenal glands are unremarkable bilaterally.

Bowel:  There is a small hiatal hernia with contrast seen within the distal
esophagus which may the evidence of gastroesophageal reflux. The small bowel
is normal appearing. The patient is status post prior right hemicolectomy. 
The remainder of the large bowel appears normal.

Vessels: There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta.  The
patient is status post stenting of the right external iliac vein.

Lymph Nodes: There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

Pelvis: The bladder is unremarkable.  The sigmoid colon and rectum are normal
appearing.  There is no pelvic sidewall lymphadenopathy The patient is status
post total hysterectomy.

Osseous Structures: There are no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions seen in
the visualized osseous structures. Again seen are soft tissue calcifications
overlying the gluteal regions bilaterally. Postsurgical changes are seen in
the anterior abdominal wall. There are few small foci of gas in the anterior
abdominal wall, likely related to subcutaneous injections.

IMPRESSION: 

No acute intra-abdominal findings.

A few small foci of gas in the anterior abdominal wall likely related to
subcutaneous injections. Correlate clinically.

Small hiatal hernia with oral contrast in the distal esophagus which may be
evidence of gastroesophageal reflux.
